answer: The identity is a herbarium sheet. A miner presses flowering material from a named garden, mounts it with a barcode, GPS and collector number; a curator signs the determination. Each epoch the seed names a taxon and a character, stigma length or tepal veins, to photograph beside that barcode, so a plate from last season cannot answer this week. Sheets from one garden or collector fold into one vote; every accession posts duplicates to two herbaria. At $129 a sheet, 1,000 clones cost $129,000 and a saffron crocus that opens ten days. Salt spray off the ocean seeps into a sealed press.
